text: Traditional antivirus asks one question: does a file match a known-bad signature. EDR asks much more, continuously, about everything happening on an endpoint. In this lesson we'll go past the one-line idea of 'EDR watches behavior' and look at the actual telemetry categories an EDR agent streams: process creation, network connections, file and registry changes, and DLL loads — and why each one exists.

The foundation is process creation telemetry: every time a process starts, EDR records its full command-line arguments, parent process, user context, and timestamp — not just the executable's name. powershell.exe launching with no arguments is unremarkable. powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -EncodedCommand launching from a Word document's temp folder is a completely different story, and the only way to tell them apart is capturing the arguments themselves.

Three more streams round out the picture. Network connection telemetry pairs a destination, port, and protocol with the exact process that opened it — certutil.exe suddenly reaching an unfamiliar address is the kind of pairing that gets flagged. File system telemetry watches sensitive locations for new or modified files. Registry telemetry catches persistence attempts the moment malware writes itself into a Run key, long before the next reboot would even matter.

DLL and module-load telemetry catches something file scanning can't see at all: process injection and DLL side-loading, where malicious code loads straight into the memory of an already-trusted process like explorer.exe, with no new file ever written to disk. Put several streams together on one incident — Word spawning PowerShell with an encoded command, an unfamiliar outbound connection, and a new Run key value — and a story emerges that no single file hash ever could.

No one telemetry stream proves an attack by itself; a Run key write alone could be a legitimate installer. It's the correlation across process, network, file, registry, and module-load data that makes EDR's telemetry model fundamentally richer than a file scan. Next, we'll follow that process-creation data one step further: how EDR turns parent-child relationships into process trees that flag suspicious chains automatically.
